steps.title: Ice wine
steps.body: Ice wine grapes must freeze naturally on the vine, usually at minus 7 to minus 13 degrees, often in December or January. Picking happens at night while frozen. The press releases only small amounts of concentrated juice, sometimes 15% of normal. Canada uses Vidal and Riesling; Germany and Austria use mainly Riesling.

steps.title: Passito
steps.body: Passito wines are made from grapes dried after harvest. Methods vary: on straw mats, in ventilated lofts, or hanging. Vin Santo is dried for months, then aged for years in small, sealed barrels called caratelli, with some oxidation. Passito di Pantelleria uses Zibibbo, a Muscat, dried in the sun.
steps.highlight: Dried on mats, lofts or racks

steps.prompt: Match each wine to its method.
steps.explanation: Different traditions concentrate sugar in different ways.

steps.body: Vin Santo with cantucci biscuits is a Tuscan ritual: dip the biscuit in the wine. The wine's nutty, dried fruit notes match the almonds.

steps.prompt: Why is ice wine picked at night?
steps.explanation: Grapes must stay frozen until pressed so the water remains as ice.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Ice wine grapes freeze naturally and are pressed while frozen
Passito grapes are dried after picking
Vin Santo, Recioto and Pantelleria are classic passito wines
